A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same S-Adam research work, with readable text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–G. Both have 21 pages; pages 2–21 have identical extracted text and rendered content.

before.justification: v1 reports original quantization-aware training and small-batch learning experiments, including accuracy, convergence times, ablations, and training curves in Section 6 and Appendix G.

after.justification: v2 retains the original experimental results in Section 6 and Appendix G, including all accuracy tables, convergence times, ablations, and training curves.

M1.justification: The LGI estimator, randomized geometric probing, exponential damping, and S-Adam updates in Section 4 and Algorithm 1 are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same synthetic examples, QAT benchmarks on CIFAR-100, TinyImageNet, Imagewoof2-160, and ImageNet, and small-batch experiments on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and Imagewoof2-160.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the corresponding experiments. AdamW and Prox-SGD remain the main baselines, and Table 5 retains the same learning-rate comparison against AdamW.

E3.justification: Quantization bit widths, architectures, batch sizes, training budgets, learning-rate settings, and reporting of best test accuracy across epochs are unchanged in Section 6 and Appendix G.

E4.justification: The damping, probe-count, and perturbation-scale ablations in Table 2, batch-size analysis in Table 4, learning-rate sensitivity in Table 5, and supplementary loss curves are identical.

E5.justification: Section 6.3 retains the same fixed-seed disclosure, seed 42. Repeated-run information and uncertainty reporting are unchanged, with no added confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: The abstract changes the reported gains from +6% to +4.54% on CIFAR-100 and from +3% to +4.27% on TinyImageNet. The new figures match unchanged Table 1 QAT differences: 18.67−14.13 against Prox-SGD and 23.18−18.91 against AdamW, respectively, using S-Adam with k=8. All underlying tables and curves remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, assumptions, convergence analysis, and proofs in Sections 3–5 and Appendices A–F are identical.

C1.justification: The abstract lowers the headline CIFAR-100 improvement and raises the TinyImageNet improvement. The methodological contributions, convergence claims, and broader empirical-superiority claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning geometric damping, gradient chattering, relative curvature, and computational trade-offs are unchanged. No substantive applicability qualifications or limitations are added or removed.

D1.justification: Section 6.3 and Appendix G retain identical implementation disclosures, NVIDIA A800 hardware information, and hyperparameter tables. No code or data access information changes.

R1.justification: Section 2, the reference list, and the positioning relative to proximal methods, smoothing, adaptive optimizers, and geometry-aware methods are unchanged.

P1.justification: Edits are confined to the abstract's numerical summary and the first-page arXiv version/date stamp. The remaining prose, terminology, section order, and appendix structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: The revised abstract causes slight first-page line wrapping and vertical-spacing changes, alongside the updated margin stamp. All figures, tables, and captions are unchanged; pages 2–21 render identically.

improvement.justification: The revised abstract gives exact gains traceable to Table 1, improving numerical consistency with the QAT results. This is a limited reporting improvement: the abstract still leaves the particular settings and different comparator baselines implicit, while the underlying experiments, methods, and proofs are unchanged.
